channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Commanders signed WR Malik Heath to the practice squad.
item.description: Heath worked out for the Commanders Wednesday and signed to the practice squad. He caught 31 passes for 308 yards and three touchdowns over the past three seasons with the Packers and spent some time with the Falcons as well last season. The Commanders add Heath as receiving depth for the practice squad.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Daiyan Henley (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description: Henley infamously was sent back to the Chargers after a reported trade with Denver fell through due to a failed physical. He returned to play in the Chargers’ Week 10 win over the Ravens, but now misses the first practice of the week with a knee issue. Given he has been playing through soreness, Henley’s absence may just be load management after a Monday game. Henley still has a chance to play in Week 11 with practices later in the week.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Ladd McConkey (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: McConkey has been dealing with the back injury for two weeks now, sitting out the Chargers’ last two games. He continues to deal with a various set of injuries and is a wild card when it comes to playing on game days. A limited designation at least gives fantasy managers hope that he will play in Week 11 against the Jets, though McConkey has fallen to unreliable WR3 status at this point of the season.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Charlie Kolar (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description: Kolar seemingly came out of the Chargers’ first win of the season with a concussion, though he was on the field up until making the game-sealing catch on the last drive. He will need to clear concussion protocol in order to be eligible for Week 11 against the Jets. Also not practicing was WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring). Neither player has fantasy impact, though Kolar’s blocking is important for a Chargers team with a banged-up offensive line.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Dre Greenlaw (neck) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description: Greenlaw popped up on the injury report with a neck issue and did not practice on Wednesday. He dealt with a knee issue last week but played through it in Week 10. Practice reports later in the week will clarify the severity of Greenlaw’s neck issue as his Week 11 status is in jeopardy for now.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Waddle exited the Broncos’ Week 9 game against the Panthers with a concussion. He had time to work through the protocol with a Week 10 bye and is now back to practicing at the start of Week 11. Given his full participant listing, Waddle is trending to play this week against the Raiders. He has had a disappointing fantasy season and should be in the WR3 ranks for Week 11.-Aditya Fuldeore

item.title: Zack Baun (back) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description: Baun watched practice from the sidelines in street clothes today. He was briefly the subject of trade rumors at the deadline, but nothing materialized. Baun will play if healthy this week, but we don’t expect him to be rushed back in the midst of a lost season for the team. He has 65 combined tackles, two sacks, and five pass breakups this year.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description: It sounds like Smith is on track to play in Week 11 against the Eagles, but it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow or Friday. Smith also told reporters today that he was 100 percent healthy for the Eagles’ Week 6 game against the Panthers, but he managed to strain his hamstring again anyway. If active, he will be a WR2 with six teams on bye, catching passes from Joe Milton.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Donatyvion Wicks (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters he feels “pretty good” about Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) returning this week. Unfortunately for both wideouts, they will rejoin an offense now led by Joe Milton. With Smith commanding a massive target share and Makai Lemon in the mix for opportunities, Wicks will be relegated to the WR5 ranks if he suits up this week.-Kyle Dvorchak

item.title: Will Shipley (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description: Shipley was designated to return from injured reserve on Monday. He can be officially activated at any time. Shipley will reclaim his RB2 role once healthy, though we don’t expect much fantasy value to come of it.-Kyle Dvorchak
